the_signal.headline: Prompt testing frameworks now separate production AI from guesswork
the_signal.body: n8n's systematic prompt testing patterns catch regressions before deployment—this is the missing link between building AI workflows and shipping them reliably. GTM engineers running AI-powered automations can't afford silent prompt degradation; structured testing turns hunches into signals. This shifts AI workflow quality from post-mortems to pre-flight checks.

tool_drop.why: GTM teams testing autonomous agent behavior on production-like constraints without burning cloud budget—useful for prototyping lead qualification or outreach agents before scaling.

thread_of_day.title: iPaaS vs. API Management: What Engineers Choose When Both Fall Short
thread_of_day.takeaway: Teams needing execution control and self-hosting requirements skip traditional iPaaS/API management layers entirely and reach for workflow platforms with code-level extensibility instead.

quote.text: Still guessing if your prompts work? Learn how to build a systematic prompt testing framework that catches regressions before they reach production.
quote.source: n8n Blog – Prompt Testing Frameworks for Production AI Workflows

whats_moving.context: Production AI workflows now require regression testing frameworks, not just load testing—this is table stakes for reliability.
Free-tier deployments (Cloudflare) are enabling GTM teams to prototype autonomous agents without committing to vendor lock-in or enterprise costs.
Breaking API changes are now caught by contract testing *inside* automation platforms, not in CI/CD—catching failures earlier in the execution chain.

act_on_this: Audit one critical AI workflow powering lead scoring or outreach—does it have systematic prompt testing or just manual checks? If manual, sketch out a regression test suite this week.
